newsitem.title: JAPAN: Burger King hopes to whet appetite of Japanese.
newsitem.headline: Burger King hopes to whet appetite of Japanese.

text.p: Burger King has taken its time entering Japan's fast-food industry, but its officials are confident it can get its teeth into a hefty chunk of the market currently dominated by rivals such as McDonald's.
The world's second-largest hamburger chain spent the past few years probing Japan's $50 billion hamburger industry through franchises operated by Seibu Railway Co.
"The test marketing has gone reasonably well," Burger King Corp chief executive officer Robert Lowes told reporters on Thursday.

The potential of the Japanese market encouraged the firm to form Burger King Japan, a 50-50 joint venture between Japan Tobacco Inc (JT) and Britain's Grand Metropolitan Plc. GrandMet is the parent company of Burger King Corp, which is based in the United States.

In order to provide outlets, JT took over the fast food division of Restaurant Morinaga Co, a wholly owned unit of confectioner Morinaga and Co. Officials said 48 of the 50 existing Morinaga Love fast-food stores were being converted into Burger Kings, to speed expansion.
"Our first objective is to successfully complete the transformation of Morinaga Love that JT acquired," said David Chapman, Burger King's managing director and vice president for the Asia Pacific.
But he added that for the company's business to really take off, at least 200 outlets were needed.
Lowes said Burger King had been offered several proposals from Japanese firms eager to enter the burger business, but declined to reveal details.

Archrival McDonald's Co (Japan) Ltd has been conducting a fierce price-cutting campaign, slashing hamburger prices to as low as 80 yen ($0.72), but Burger King officials, with their cheapest burger at priced at 220 yen ($2), are not worried.

"What we want to do is to bring the best burger and with value that does not necessarily mean the lowest price," Lowes said. "The Japanese consumer has shown willingess to pay incremental amounts for good quality."

He added that the Haagen-Dazs ice cream brand was unknown seven years ago, but it is now the largest premium brand ice cream in Japan, thanks to choosy Japanese. Haagen-Dazs Japan Inc, which operates ice cream parlours and sells ice cream, is also a member of the GrandMet family.
Burger King officials said their target clientele was mainly young females, ranging between 18 and 23 years of age.
"Japan has a wide variety of food to choose from and a great number of females are attracted to our restaurants," a Burger King Japan marketing manager said.
"In the U.S. it is slightly slanted towards males."
At the moment, Burger King is selling its Whopper hamburgers and french fries at five directly owned outlets in Tokyo, which it hopes to expand to 35 by the end of the calendar year, Chapman said.
Other items, such as onion rings and salads, could be added to the menu within 18 months, he said. ($1=111 yen)
